source_checks.finding: Cited page 'Report spam and block senders in Messages on iPhone' was not returned by search; the page returned by search for that identifier is the Apple iPhone User Guide section 'Block, filter, and report messages' (iph3f94d910d). Section 'Report spam messages' confirms: 'Open Messages on your iPhone.' 'Swipe left on the conversation, then tap the Delete icon.' 'Tap Delete and Report Spam to report and delete it.' 'You can't report a message after you've replied to it.' For SMS, MMS, or RCS spam the page says to contact your carrier if you don't see the reporting option. 'Reporting spam doesn't prevent the sender from sending messages.' To stop their messages, block the contact. Applies to iPhone. The ref excerpt 'Delete and Report Spam' is exact. Note: an earlier version of the page (iph203ab0be4) says 'Delete and Report Junk' instead, so the iph3f94d910d version is the one to cite.

Page is for Google Messages on Android and is correctly not used: the user has an iPhone, so this is a distractor. Exact menu wording on the page is 'Block & report spam' in the 'Block from inside a conversation' steps (More options, Details, Block & report spam, OK), and 'Block', 'Report spam', 'OK' from the conversation list; the ref's excerpt 'Block & report spam' is therefore a valid label.

source_checks.finding: Page 'Report spam in Google Messages' (Android, Google Messages). Steps: 'Touch and hold the conversation you want to report.' 'Tap Block' then 'Report spam' then 'OK.' 'Sending reports is optional.' 'You can also block a phone number and don't have to report it to Google.' 'The spammer's phone number is reported to Google.' 'The last 10 incoming messages from the spammer are reported to Google.' The page also says: 'When you report a conversation as spam, you also block the sender and move the message to your Spam & blocked folder.' The ref excerpt 'Block & report spam' is a menu option that appears in the 'Block from inside a conversation' steps, not the section heading 'Block & report a conversation' the ref names. Applies to this Android user.

Page 'How to Recognize and Report Spam Text Messages' (found by search; the cited articles/how-recognize-and-report-spam-text-messages address was not returned). Exact words: 'Copy the message and forward it to 7726 (SPAM).' Also 'Report it to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.' (under 'How To Report Spam Text Messages'). The page's 'What To Do About Spam Text Messages' section says: 'If you get a text message you weren't expecting and it asks you to give some personal or financial information, don't click on any links.' and 'If you think the message might be real, contact the company using a phone number or website you know is real.' The ref's own applicability (any phone) is correct; the page is general. Card-level note: the passage drops the 'If you think the message might be real' condition from the 'contact the company' advice and states it unconditionally; the target does not use that advice, so the target is unaffected.

Apple iPhone page (found by search for identifier iph3f94d910d). Applies to iPhone and is correctly not used: the user is on Android, so this is a distractor. Exact words in the 'Report spam messages' section: 'Delete and Report Spam', with 'You can't report a message after you've replied to it.'
